items.label: 1B
items.claim: A buyer group that does real volume (NAO wastewater, 37+ runs) reports negotiating only about 15% off the 25B list price, which is modest discounting at a mid-size account.
items.detail: The post (jefftk, cross-posted to LessWrong, 26 Jun 2025) gives a 25B 2x150 list price of $16,480 and says groups have negotiated discounts around 15%. At 15% the net is $16,480 x 0.85 = $14,008 per flow cell, or about $1.59/Gb on the observed 8,800 Gb average. This is a watch-out for 1B: the evidence is one anecdote, but it shows no sign of 'insane' discounts below the largest accounts. It is also consistent with the thesis that the discount gap is concentrated in the largest accounts.
items.source_name: LessWrong / jefftk (Jeff Kaufman), NAO wastewater sequencing
items.why_new: The exclusion list has a $16,480 / ~15% write-up only as a practitioner datapoint (F141); this adds the author, date and observed-yield arithmetic.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Observed 25B output beats the advertised spec, so the effective $/Gb is lower than the list price implies, which is hidden deflation.
items.detail: The post's measured averages are 29.4B read pairs (about 8,800 Gb, n=37 runs at BCL) and 27.2B (about 8,200 Gb, n=4 at MU). Both are at or above the 8,000 Gb spec (+10% and +2.5%). At list, $16,480 / 8,800 = $1.87/Gb, against $2.06/Gb on spec, so customers get about 9% more data per dollar than the price sheet shows. Older MU runs were about 20% lower, which suggests yield rose over time, so effective price per Gb fell with no list-price cut.
items.why_new: The known list gives only spec-based $/Gb and a Texas A&M '30% more output' anecdote; this adds measured per-run yields (n=37 and n=4) and a ~20% older-run lag.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Yield on 25B flow cells has been rising over time, a second source of unpriced $/Gb decline.
items.detail: The author says older MU runs were about 20% below the current 27.2B read-pair average, which implies roughly 21.8B pairs earlier. The 25% gain from 21.8B to 27.2B is a de facto price cut of 1 - 1/1.25 = 20% per Gb at an unchanged list price. This is a small sample (n=4 at MU) at one sequencing center, so treat it as directional.
items.why_new: Gives a quantified, dated yield improvement on a single core, extending the known 'hidden $/Gb deflation' point.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Usable data per flow cell is only about 60% of raw output in a real workflow, so adjusted cost per usable Gb is much higher and the real constraint is not raw sequencing price.
items.detail: Adapter trimming keeps about 60% of raw bases, because median read length falls from 300 bp to about 170 bp. That lifts cost from $1.87/Gb raw to $3.30/Gb usable (the post's figure, about 1.8x). For this wastewater use case, the cost lever is sample prep and read design more than flow-cell price. That is consistent with the thesis that sequencing cost is no longer the sole constraint, but it is one non-clinical, non-Illumina-revenue-representative workload.
items.why_new: Quantifies the raw-to-usable gap (60%) for a metagenomic workload, not previously in the file.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina's cost advantage over nanopore is large (about 100x per Gb in this use case), which limits switching pressure from ONT.
items.detail: On PromethION flow cells at $900 in bulk, the author observed only 3.3 Gb per flow cell (n=25), against marketed '>200 Gb', or about $272/Gb. Illumina 25B at $1.87-3.30/Gb is therefore nearly two orders of magnitude cheaper for wastewater metagenomics. This cuts against the idea that every rival platform is eroding Illumina pricing, at least in metagenomics and on this author's protocols.
items.why_new: The known list covers ONT's per-genome pricing, not observed wastewater yield versus claims.

notes: The post was opened. The fetch tool returned a summary rather than the full text, and I did not re-read the original. The post is one practitioner anecdote, with no 6000, 10B or Ultima/Element comparison. The author is Jeff Kaufman of the NAO. The $16,480 list price differs from the known Jan 2025 Illumina kit prices (25B-300 $24,155, 200-cycle $14,500), so it is probably a 2x150 reseller or quote price. One could check the NAO's other posts (jefftk.com, data.securebio.org) for prior flow-cell prices.
